evidence.subtitlePartner: The research, data, and architecture behind Steel Man Resumes.
evidence.subtitleClient: The research and data that powers your results.
evidence.observer: You're seeing a summary. The full evidence deck with citations, competitive analysis, and architecture decisions is available to partner organizations.
evidence.gapPartner: The Gap: What No Other Tool Does

finding.0: fMRI study showing that putting feelings into words reduces amygdala reactivity by up to 50%.
finding.1: Affect labeling outperforms cognitive reappraisal and distraction in reducing emotional reactivity.
finding.2: Self-efficacy is built through mastery experiences (real accomplishments), not encouragement or verbal persuasion.
finding.3: The Transtheoretical Model describes five stages of change. Intervention effectiveness depends on matching the user’s current stage.
finding.4: Redemption sequences (bad→good narrative arcs) predict higher well-being and generativity.
finding.5: Desistance from crime correlates with constructing a ‘generative identity’: seeing oneself as someone who can contribute positively.
finding.6: Autonomy, competence, and relatedness are core psychological needs. Autonomy-supportive environments produce better outcomes.
finding.7: Scaffolding: provide structure that fades as competence grows. More support early, less later.
finding.8: Process praise (‘You worked hard on that’) builds growth mindset. Person praise (‘You’re smart’) builds fixed mindset.

gap.0: No integrated AI + legal navigation for justice-impacted populations
gap.1: No research-grounded behavioral framework for career AI
gap.2: No decision observability in career tools
gap.3: No scaffolded career exploration for low-digital-literacy users

why.did: Employers are scanning for what you handled, not what the job description said. Your own plain words are the raw material. They do not need to be polished.
why.tools: Naming the equipment or system is the fastest proof you have actually done the work, and tools are exactly what employer software searches for.
why.often: Frequency turns a duty into a scale. "Ran the crusher pit" and "ran the crusher pit every shift" are two different claims, and only one of them is specific.
why.quantity: One real number does more than a page of description, and it is the thing almost no resume has. It does not need to be impressive. It needs to be true and yours.
why.improved: This is the line between what you were assigned and what you changed. It is the hardest question here and usually the most valuable answer.

stage.precontemplation: No pressure here. Answer whatever comes easily and skip the rest. Even one answer is enough to work with.
stage.contemplation: Answer what you can, in your own words. Even one answer is enough to start, and you can come back to the others.
stage.preparation: Answer in your own words. We use only what you tell us, and nothing gets invented.
stage.action: The more specific you get here, the harder this lands with an employer. Numbers especially.

ph.did: e.g., loaded trucks and kept track of inventory
ph.often: e.g., every shift, daily, during peak season
ph.quantity: How many people, orders or loads? Only if you know.
ph.improved: e.g., fewer mistakes, faster loading, kept the team on schedule
